stories.head: True Anomaly bags $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly raised $190 million in a Series C round, valuing the company at $1.6 billion. The funding emphasizes the growing demand for co-orbital security and space domain awareness, especially as geopolitical tensions rise. With DoD pull-through becoming a headline, the market is clearly betting on a future filled with more threats and more satellites.
stories.soWhat: Investors are clearly convinced that space security is the next big thing, but it’s worth noting that the hype often overshadows the actual capabilities.

stories.head: Rocket Lab launches 10th Synspective satellite
stories.body: Rocket Lab successfully launched its 10th Synspective satellite, showcasing its reliability in the small satellite launch market. This mission adds to a growing fleet aimed at Earth observation, despite the company's ongoing struggles with rocket landings. With each successful launch, Rocket Lab inches closer to solidifying its position against competitors like SpaceX.
stories.soWhat: Reliability in launches is becoming the new currency; Rocket Lab's ability to deliver consistently may set it apart in a crowded field.

stories.head: ISS repair highlights station's deteriorating health
stories.body: NASA astronauts are preparing for a spacewalk to repair a robotic arm on the International Space Station, raising alarms about the station's long-term viability. As repairs become more frequent, questions linger about whether the ISS can sustain its operational status for much longer. The ISS, once a symbol of international cooperation, is now a patchwork of quick fixes.
stories.soWhat: The ISS may soon become a liability rather than an asset; if the repairs keep piling up, the future of human spaceflight might need a new stage.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
